Read History Go to My Account Log Out Agriculture FG supports 3,520 flood-hit Kogi farmers with farm inputs The federal government is providing fertilisers, improved rice seeds and agrochemicals to 3,520 farmers affected by flooding in Kogi State
Listen to this article Share The federal government is providing fertilisers, improved rice seeds and agrochemicals to 3,520 farmers affected by flooding in Kogi State as part of efforts to restore agricultural production and protect farmers’ livelihoods. Advertisement Advertisement The intervention is being implemented through the National Agricultural Development Fund (NADF) under its 2026 Flood Recovery Agricultural Inputs Intervention, which was launched in Lokoja. The beneficiaries are expected to receive urea and NPK fertilisers, 15kg bags of rice seeds, pre-planting, pre-emergence and early post-emergence chemicals, as well as insecticides to support the resumption of farming activities. Speaking at the launch, Mohammed Ibrahim, executive secretary and chief executive officer of NADF represented by Muhammad Gidado, the fund’s team lead in Kogi State, said the programme reflected the Federal Government’s commitment to agricultural resilience, farmers’ welfare and sustainable food production. He said the intervention would help farmers recover from flood-related losses, restore their livelihoods and return to production, while supporting national food security. “This intervention is more than the distribution of agricultural inputs; it is a demonstration of solidarity with our farmers and a collective commitment to restoring hope, protecting livelihoods and securing the future of agriculture in Nigeria,” Gidado said. Advertisement He urged the Kogi State Government, community leaders and other stakeholders to ensure that the inputs were distributed transparently and promptly to the intended beneficiaries. Gidado also advised farmers to use the materials appropriately to achieve the programme’s recovery objectives. Advertisement Timothy Ojomah, kogi state commissioner for Agriculture and Food Security, said the state was among six beneficiaries of the Federal Government’s flood recovery programme. He described the intervention as timely, given Kogi’s recurring exposure to flooding, and thanked President Bola Tinubu, Abubakar Kyari, Minister of Agriculture and Food Security, and the NADF leadership for extending the support to the state. Advertisement Advertisement Ojomah assured that the state government would monitor the distribution and use of the inputs, warning beneficiaries against selling or diverting the materials. “I urge beneficiaries to guard against diverting or selling the agricultural inputs,” he said. “Any inputs given to our farmers will be used judiciously. Our farmers need more, so selling is not an option here in Kogi,” he added. George Bello, managing director of the Kogi State Agricultural Development Project (ADP), described the intervention as a lifeline for farmers struggling to recover from flood damage. He said the ADP would complement the distribution with extension services to guide beneficiaries on the proper application and use of the fertilisers, seeds and chemicals. According to him, the support and technical guidance would help farmers maximise the benefits of the intervention. He also cautioned beneficiaries against selling the inputs. Abanika Taiye, kogi state Commissioner for Housing and Urban Development, said the programme complemented the agricultural initiatives of Ahmed Usman Ododo, governor of the state. Taiye noted that flooding had left many farmers in difficult circumstances, adding that the Federal Government’s intervention had provided relief and renewed hope to affected communities. “Farmers are in a disheartening situation. They are not happy. But with this now, this has brought them succour, and that is going to increase agricultural production in the state,” he said.
